resolved_findings: Producer/generation scoped outcome identity and complete write-set duplicate equality prevent cross-producer event aliasing or altered-effect retries from borrowing a success
Explicit review update remains independent of delivery/history and retained unresolved obligations; registration checks run/harness/generation
Full u64 values use checked eight-byte BLOB encoding; transaction writes and producer/global checkpoints commit together, with bounded capacity and rollback behavior

Live restore uses a revision above both current and backup; explicit corrupt-page recovery requires authoritative upper bound including unknown committed revisions, identifiable supported main header and no pending WAL
Startup retirement also passes WAL pressure; failed/busy post-commit checkpoint cannot replace a successful committed response
History cap maintenance is bounded and distinct from tombstones, protected obligations and outbox audit; tombstone removal retires the affected current generation atomically
Worker permits cover queued/executing/completed retained receipts; rejected submission returns exact request, timeout or disconnect never claims rollback, explicit recovery timeout may have committed

Shared crate-private generation helper reuses the existing entropy code without protocol I/O, a storage-to-ingestion dependency, new public API or new dependency; both callers preserve their existing sanitized error categories
Filesystem/SQLite descriptor-anchor behavior and same-UID limits are documented; fixed standalone backup sidecars and staged known migration corrected as separately reviewed

accepted_exceptions: 54-line shallow declarative verification plan: three branches, nesting one; keeping a single required-check inventory avoids parallel fragments
One retention integration fixture has 56 lexical/54 Clippy lines with a specific expect: it follows history/tombstone/obligation lifetimes together. No production or blanket suppression
maintainability.responsibilities: One worker/connection; explicit transport/permits, types/validation, fixed path ownership, schema/configuration, transactions, bounded queries, maintenance and supported backup/recovery. Protocol stays pure; no arbitrary SQL/callback seam exposed.
